title: Coefficient sheaves on the geometric point
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be separably closed and $X=\Spec\Omega$. For a condensed set or
condensed ring $F$, $(p_X^*F)(\Omega[S])\cong F(S)$ naturally in the profinite set
$S$. In particular:

1. for a topological ring $T$ (for instance profinite or locally profinite),
   $\underline T_X(\Omega[S])=C(S,T)$, the continuous functions;
2. for a discrete ring $A$, $\underline A_X(\Omega[S])=LC(S,A)=\varinjlim_iA^{S_i}$,
   which is $(\nu_X^*A_{X,\Et})(\Omega[S])$; so $\underline A_X$ is the classical
   constant sheaf.

proof.text: Put $u(S)=\Omega[S]$. By [det-pe-condensed-point-basis], $u$ identifies profinite sets with the affine ind-étale objects over $X$. The homeomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum], specialized to the field $\Omega$, identifies $|u(S)|$ with $S$: the point $s$ is $\ker(\operatorname{ev}_s)$. Precomposition with $f:T\to S$ sends the prime at $t$ to the prime at $f(t)$, so $|u(f)|=f$. Every arrow between these objects is weakly étale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. By the covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], a covering of the affine $u(S)$ has finitely many affine opens in its sources whose images cover $u(S)$; their finitely many source objects are therefore jointly surjective. Conversely finitely many jointly surjective affine sources are a covering: for any affine open $V\subset u(S)$, its inverse images in these affine sources are affine (they are fibre products of affine schemes over the affine $u(S)$), and cover $V$. Thus the induced covering families are exactly those containing a finite jointly surjective subfamily, as in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring].

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], every object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is covered by affine ind-étale objects, and their fibre products remain in the basis. The functor $u$ is fully faithful by [det-pe-condensed-point-basis], and Step 1 identifies its induced topology with the coherent topology. Apply [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] to $u$, first with sets and then with abelian groups: restriction $R(G)(S)=G(\Omega[S])$ is an equivalence in both cases. The stated small-site universe convention is used, so the required right Kan extension limits exist in sets and abelian groups in the larger universe.

source.place: First paragraph, equivalence-of-topoi input; Topoi paragraph of sk-prop-pe-condensed-point-topology.proof.md

proof.text: For abelian sheaves, [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] identifies $p_X^*$ as left adjoint to $R$, since $X[S]=\Omega[S]$ by [det-pe-condensed-point-basis]. For sets use the geometric inverse image of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]: its right adjoint is the composite restriction, which on $S$ evaluates $G$ at $\operatorname{Spec}LC(S,\mathbf Z)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X=X[S]$, hence is again $R$. A left adjoint of the equivalence $R$ is its inverse: if $Q$ is an inverse, the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(QF,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(F,RG)$ identify $Q$ with $p_X^*$ by the adjunction universal property. Its unit $\eta_F:F\to Rp_X^*F$ is therefore invertible, giving the asserted evaluation naturally in $F$ and $S$. For a ring $F$, apply the set inverse image to its finite-arity operations. Naturality of $\eta$ at addition and multiplication, together with its product projections, gives $\eta_F(a+b)=\eta_F(a)+\eta_F(b)$ and $\eta_F(ab)=\eta_F(a)\eta_F(b)$; its zero-arity operation gives $\eta_F(1)=1$. This is the ring inverse image, equivalently the strong monoidal ring-object construction of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Thus the evaluation is a ring isomorphism as well.

source.place: First paragraph, adjunction and ring-structure argument

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], the evaluation just proved gives $\underline T_X(\Omega[S])=C(S,T)$ with pointwise ring operations. For discrete $A$, continuity means exactly local constancy. Index $S_i$ by the finite continuous quotient sets of $S$ ordered by refinement. A continuous $a:S\to A$ has finite image because its open fibres cover the compact $S$; those fibres give a finite clopen quotient, so $a$ is the pullback of an element of $A^{S_i}$. If two finite-stage functions have equal pullbacks, their pullbacks to the common quotient given by nonempty intersections of their fibres agree, because $S$ surjects onto that quotient. Thus $C(S,A)=LC(S,A)=\varinjlim_i A^{S_i}$ as rings. This construction commutes with a continuous map $T\to S$ by precomposition and the induced refinements. For $S=\varnothing$ the empty quotient gives the one-element zero ring on both sides.

source.place: Second paragraph, continuous and locally constant sections

proof.text: The test-object formula of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] and [det-pe-condensed-point-basis] gives $\Omega[S]=\varprojlim_i U_i$, where $U_i=\coprod_{s\in S_i}X=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega^{S_i}$ and the transitions are induced by the quotient maps. Each $U_i$ is affine étale of finite presentation over $X$: $\Omega^{S_i}=\prod_{s\in S_i}\Omega$ is finitely presented, and each factor is the localization $\Omega^{S_i}[e_s^{-1}]$ at the idempotent $e_s$, so $U_i$ is a finite disjoint union of open subschemes each mapping isomorphically to $X$ (this is the converse of clause (1) of the basis node, not that clause itself). By [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable], the constant étale sheaf with underlying set $A$ is represented by $\coprod_{a\in A}X$. An $X$-map from $U_i$ to this coproduct chooses one component for each $s\in S_i$, since each $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ has one point. Hence $A_{X,\mathrm{Et}}(U_i)=A^{S_i}$. The constant sheaf definition [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] equips these sections with the original constants on each component; gluing the components gives pointwise addition, multiplication and unit, also for a noncommutative ring. For a map of finite sets the scheme map sends each component to its specified component, so restriction is exactly precomposition. This proves the finite-stage evaluation with its ring operations and transition maps, including $S_i=\varnothing$.

source.place: Second paragraph, finite affine presentation and finite-stage constant-sheaf evaluations

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections] with affine $X=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, the presentation of Step 5, and the underlying abelian étale sheaf of $A_{X,\mathrm{Et}}$ (a sheaf of $\mathbf Z$-modules). It gives $(\nu_X^*A_{X,\mathrm{Et}})(\Omega[S])=\varinjlim_i A^{S_i}$ naturally in the basis object. The formula sends a finite-stage section to its restriction; Step 5 shows that restrictions preserve multiplication and unit, so the formula is a ring isomorphism. Together with Steps 3–4 this gives an isomorphism of the two restricted ring sheaves. The basis detection and uniqueness statement of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] extends it uniquely to an isomorphism on the full site, with its inverse and operation identities extending by the same uniqueness. To verify the last constant-sheaf assertion directly, $LC(S,A)$ is the constant sheaf of rings on the profinite site: a ring homomorphism $A\to H(*)$ to the sections of any ring sheaf $H$ defines a map $LC(S,A)\to H(S)$ by pulling its value $a$ back to each clopen fibre of a locally constant function and gluing over this finite covering; refinement of partitions makes this natural and unique. Conversely such a sheaf map is determined by its component at $*$ and has that construction, so it satisfies the sheafification universal property in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Under the equivalence of Step 2, final-object sections are preserved, since $u(*)=X$. The same universal property therefore identifies $\underline A_X$ with the constant ring sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$.
